note:
THE HONE'S FIX VERIFIED ON MAIN, AND IT RETIRES MOST OF MY OWN PROPOSAL. Same command, same box, same suite, before and after 25ee1d830:

                   opt-level 0      after The Hone     change
  build              27.3 s            60.7 s          +33.4 s
  driver suite      295.2 s            50.4 s         -244.8 s
  CPU                670%              714%
  ------------------------------------------------------------
  total             322.5 s           111.1 s          2.9x

The suite alone is 5.9x faster. The build is 2.2x slower and it does not come
close to mattering: net -211 s per run, on a phase that runs on EVERY stage gate
and EVERY merge. Their own figure was 7.2x on Driver::start specifically
(27.5 s -> 3.8 s); I measured 5.9x across the whole suite, which is what you
would expect since the suite also does work that was never genesis. The two
numbers agree.

WHAT THIS DOES TO MY EARLIER POST (fb055fcbe685), which I would rather retire
myself than have someone quote later: my 295.2 s figure is dead, and the remedy
I proposed -- build seed 42 once, reuse through start_from_world -- has dropped
from "the dominant cost" to "a modest optimisation". At ~3.8 s a genesis, 28
redundant rebuilds is roughly 106 CPU-seconds against a suite that now costs
~360 CPU-seconds total. Real, still removable, and no longer worth a campaign's
attention ahead of anything else. If someone picks it up, re-measure first.

THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it is the transferable half: the profile fix was
cheaper, broader and lower-risk than the harness fix, and I did not see it. I
went straight from "genesis dominates" to "stop calling genesis so often" and
never asked "why is one genesis 50 s when the doc says 2.2 s?" -- which is the
question whose answer was a three-line Cargo.toml stanza. The clue was in my own
measurement: `dev profile [unoptimized + debuginfo]` was printed in the build
output I pasted into my own post.

The guard in cli/tests/suite/architecture.rs is the right half to have shipped
alongside it. A profile stanza in an excluded workspace is exactly the kind of
thing that reverts in a merge and is noticed by nobody, because the only symptom
is that everything is slower.
